told_more: The record gave me dates, causes, uses and who did what, and it separates original from copied and neglected from kept; the views gave none of that. The views are bare clay with no paint colour, so repaints, paint age and weathering cannot be seen at all. What the views do confirm is the openings: A's shopfront is there in 1989, 2000 and 2010 and gone in 2020 (three windows matching the upper ones); B has no shopfront in 1989 and a blank-panelled one in 2000 (a balcony and glazed annex by 2010); C's upper gable window gains a frame between 1989 and 2000, and its lane-side ground-floor windows change only in 2020; D is boarded in 1989 and 2000 and glazed in 2010 and 2020; E is glazed in 1989 and 2000 and boarded in 2010 and 2020. Those are only a few of the record's events, and they say nothing of why. The views mostly add spatial sense: the arrangement, scale and what is boarded.

contradicts.claim: House B's 2003 'balcony over the lane' appears as a balcony with railing over a glazed, enclosed ground-floor annex (a sun-room or veranda volume) that bulges into the lane mouth; the record lists only a balcony and no enclosed ground-floor extension.

House A has an upper-floor bay or oriel window at the left of the quay-road front in all four years; the record lists only a jugend house with a mansard roof and no bay, so I could not say whether it is original or a later addition.

House B's 1997 bakery shopfront (2000, 2010, 2020) is a blank, opaque panel with a door and no shop glass, so it reads as shuttered, closed or boarded rather than as an open bakery; there is also an unexplained black rectangle on the wall above it, probably a sign, which the record does not describe.
House D's roof 'lets in water' in the record from 1995 until 2007, but the roof looks intact and undamaged in the 2000 views; I see no sign of the leak or of any neglect beyond the boards.
House E is recorded as neglected and empty from 1993, but it looks identical in 1989 and 2000, with intact windows, so the views show no neglect until the boards of 2008.
From above, House B's roof looks like a ribbed, gently pitched roof with a chimney rather than a clearly flat one as the record says; the front elevation reads flat-topped, so I may be misreading it.

views_showed: At a glance the corner is mostly static over 31 years: the changes are details of openings, and the only large ones are A's shopfront removal, B's balcony and annex, and the boards on D and then on E.

The vacant boarded house moves up the lane: D is boarded in 1989 and 2000 and open in 2010 and 2020, while E at the top is boarded in 2010 and 2020 and open before, so the empty house that closes the view up the lane changes over time.

House C's windows read as more traditional and detailed (framed, many-paned) after the 1998 upper-floor copies and after the 2011 'old style' factory windows on the lane-side ground floor than the plain 1971 ones; a viewer would take the factory windows for authentic old windows, so the views cannot separate copies or factory 'old style' windows from originals.
B's balcony and glazed annex visibly narrow the mouth of the lane and project over it in 2010 and 2020.
A's 2020 ground floor regains a house front with windows echoing the upper floor, so the house reads as a house again; that return is clearer in the views than in the record.
A's shopfront looks the same in 1989, 2000 and 2010, so the closure of the shop in 2009 is invisible in the views.
The forms make age and type visible at once: A's mansard, B's modern flat-fronted box, and C, D and E as small gabled timber houses with D perched on its rock outcrop and E closing the lane.
missing: All causes, owners, dates and uses are absent from the views: ironmonger, cafe, bakery, flats, the heirs, the break-in, the oil-price fall, the city's wooden-town rules.
Repainting and paint age: A's long gap from 1949 to 1996, and the repaints of B (1987, 2003, 2017), C (1998, 2013), D (2007) and A (1996, 2016), are not visible in clay.
Neglect that is not boarding: A's shabbiness in 1989, D's leaking roof, and E's emptiness from 1993 to 2008 are not visible.
Whether a shop is open or closed: A's cafe, then its closure in 2009, and B's bakery trading.
Original fabric versus replacement, such as the 1965 and 1971 windows or whether any window is a copy, beyond small differences in frame detail; the 1950 lean-to at D is visible but undated.
B's 1935 fire and the 1884 chalet it replaced, and the original styles (jugend, Swiss chalet, empire) beyond the basic forms.
Who lives where in C: the upper flat versus the ground-floor flat and their separate owners.
